name: Blaminhor Essentials – All-in-One WordPress Toolkit
author: blaminhor

sections.description:
One plugin to replace twenty. Free forever.

I was tired of my WordPress installs looking like a graveyard of single-purpose plugins — one for SEO, one for cache, one for SMTP, one for redirects, one for backups. Each one with its own dashboard, its own freemium dance. So I built Blaminhor Essentials — and I never sell your data.

Why this plugin exists:

  • Every WordPress essential under one roof. SEO, cache, SMTP, backup, cookie banner, contact forms, calendar, anti-spam, login security, downloads, redirections, broken links, duplicator, database optimizer, domain changer, fatal error recovery, favicon, HTTPS redirect, hide login, image sizes, maintenance mode, mute core emails, post types order, user role editor, classic editor, disable comments. Switch on what you use today; the rest stays out of your way until the day you need it.
  • Your existing data comes with you. Switching does not mean starting over: built-in importers for Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, WP Mail SMTP, Post SMTP, Easy WP SMTP, Redirection, Safe Redirect Manager, Custom Taxonomy Order, Favicon by RealFaviconGenerator, and the standalone User Role Editor. The dedicated plugins you’ve stacked one by one over the years, now in a single coherent toolkit.
  • No tax for what you don’t use. Each module is independent: an inactive one registers no hooks of its own, enqueues no assets and runs no queries of its own. Only a small shared core always loads, so beyond it you’re only paying — in memory and milliseconds — for the features you actually turned on.
  • Rebuilt on modern PHP. Since version 2, every module has been re-engineered from the ground up to take full advantage of PHP 8 — strict types, enums and value objects — for tighter security and faster, leaner execution.
  • Free. All features above are free. No tracking, no telemetry.
  • Translated in 11 languages. English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese, Russian, Turkish, Dutch, Indonesian.
  • You can email me anytime. hi+wp@blaminhor.com

Available Features — 26 modules:

Performance

  • Cache & Performance — Page cache, asset optimization and lazy load, plus a Web Vitals dashboard and an auto-pilot that benchmarks each speed option on your own pages.

SEO & Links

  • SEO/GEO — Meta titles and descriptions with SERP preview, XML sitemaps, per-type indexing control, and one-click import from Yoast, Rank Math or All in One SEO.
  • Redirections — Simple or regex redirects (301, 302, 307, 410, 451) with hit counters, slug-change detection, and CSV / plugin import (Redirection, Safe Redirect Manager).
  • Broken Links — Scan posts, pages and custom post types for dead internal and external links, with live results and one-click fixes.

Emails

  • SMTP Mailer — Reliable delivery through 12+ providers (Brevo, SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES…) with automatic relay fallback, a retry queue for emails that fail (Beta), logging, and import from WP Mail SMTP, Post SMTP or Easy WP SMTP.
  • Mute Core Emails — Silence WordPress automatic notifications (updates, new users, password changes, comments) individually.

Security & Maintenance

  • Cookie Banner — Self-hosted consent banner that blocks tracking scripts and embeds until visitors agree, with GDPR/CCPA/LGPD presets, Consent Mode v2, and a 13-month consent log.
  • Anti-Spam — Block spam bots on the comment, login, registration and password forms with a hidden honeypot trap, and encode the email addresses shown on your site so harvesters cannot read them — no CAPTCHA, no external service.
  • Login Security — Lock out brute-force attempts on every sign-in route (login form, XML-RPC, REST API, application passwords) before the password is checked, add two-factor authentication (authenticator app, security key or passkey, emailed code, single-use backup codes) with trusted browsers, alert on sign-ins from unfamiliar devices, enforce a password policy per role, and keep a journal of every attempt with addresses stored hashed. Entirely local, no external service.
  • Hide Login Page — Replace wp-login.php with a custom URL and block bots probing the default login.
  • HTTPS Redirect — Force HTTPS site-wide with optional mixed-content fixing and an HSTS header.
  • Fatal Error Recovery — Recover a crashed site from a secret URL by disabling the culprit plugin, with no FTP access.
  • Maintenance — Show a Coming Soon (200) or Maintenance (503) page, with role and IP whitelisting.
  • User Role Editor — Create, clone and edit roles and capabilities, with per-user overrides, JSON import/export and one-click import from the standalone User Role Editor plugin.

Database & Migration

  • Backup & Restore — Scheduled backups of files and database as separate archives, with a safety backup and one-click undo before every restore.
  • Database Optimizer — Clean revisions, transients, spam and orphaned data on a schedule, with an at-a-glance size and overhead overview.
  • Domain Changer — Change your site domain and update every database reference, including serialized data, in one click.

Content & Media

  • Calendar — Publish events with recurrence, venues, organizers, calendar views, iCal import and RSVP, and run a full booking system for appointments and resource rentals with reminders and Stripe payments.
  • Forms — Accessible drag-and-drop contact forms with entries stored in the database, no-CAPTCHA spam protection, and GDPR controls.
  • Downloads — Count how many times each media library file is downloaded, and how many distinct people downloaded it, without recreating your files as anything else. Make documents save instead of opening in a tab, restrict a file to signed-in visitors, chosen roles or a password, and optionally route direct file requests through the counted link so links already shared are covered too. Robots, link previews and repeat clicks are filtered out, and no visitor address is ever stored.
  • Content Duplicator — Clone any post, page or custom post type with all fields, taxonomies and child posts; supports every major page builder.
  • Classic Editor & Widgets — Restore the classic editor and/or the classic widgets screen, independently.
  • Image Sizes — Disable unused thumbnail sizes, register custom ones, and regenerate existing images.
  • Favicon Generator — Generate every favicon format (PNG, Apple Touch, Android, Windows tiles) from a single square image, or import an existing set from Favicon by RealFaviconGenerator or the WordPress Site Icon.
  • Post Types Order — Reorder posts, pages, custom post types and taxonomies with drag and drop, and import an existing term order from Custom Taxonomy Order.
  • Disable Comments — Remove the comment system site-wide and hide it from the admin, reversibly.

External services

Every module is off by default, and a module that is off contacts nothing. This section lists every outside service a module can connect to, what it receives and when. Most of them start only once you enter your own account details or tick a specific option. Three start as soon as their module is turned on, and are marked “on by default” below: the Calendar venue map, and the self-hosted Google Fonts and YouTube thumbnails of Cache & Performance.

Stripe (Forms and Calendar payments)

Takes online payments for paid forms, paid event sign-ups, paid appointments and resource rentals. It is used only once you enter a Stripe secret key on the Forms settings page (Payments section), and only for the forms, events, services or resources you give a price.

When a visitor starts a payment, your server sends Stripe the amount, the currency, a short description (the form’s payment label, or the event, service or resource name), the addresses on your site the visitor comes back to, and two internal references: a random payment token and the kind of purchase. The visitor then types their card details, and any contact details Stripe asks for, on Stripe’s own payment page; none of it passes through your site. While a payment is pending, your server checks its status with Stripe when the visitor comes back, and otherwise once an hour. If a payment arrives for something that can no longer be recorded (a slot taken in the meantime, for example), your server asks Stripe to refund it.

Stripe: Services Agreement, Privacy Policy.

Google reCAPTCHA and Cloudflare Turnstile (Forms)

Optional CAPTCHA challenges against spam. Forms already blocks spam without them: a CAPTCHA is used only if you enter the provider’s keys on the Forms settings page and add a CAPTCHA field to a form.

On a page that shows such a form, the visitor’s browser loads the provider’s script from google.com or challenges.cloudflare.com. The provider therefore receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details and whatever its script collects, under its own policy. When the form is sent, your server sends the provider the challenge token and your secret key so it can check the answer; the plugin does not add the visitor’s IP address to that check.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Cloudflare: Website Terms, Privacy Policy.

Google PageSpeed Insights (Cache & Performance)

Measures how fast a page loads. It runs only when you start a PageSpeed audit in Cache & Performance → Performance, or with the matching WP-CLI command. Your server sends Google the address of the page to audit and, if you saved one, your PageSpeed API key; Google then loads that public page to measure it. Testing a key sends one request with the key and a sample address.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Cloudflare API (Cache & Performance)

Keeps Cloudflare’s cache in step with your site. It is used only if you tick “Enable Cloudflare integration” in Cache & Performance → CDN and enter an API token and a Zone ID. With your token, your server sends Cloudflare the addresses of the pages to refresh when you publish, update or trash content, a request to empty the whole zone when you empty the site cache, and, when you click the matching buttons, reads and changes of your zone’s settings (Development Mode, recommended settings).

Cloudflare: Website Terms, Privacy Policy.

Google Fonts (Cache & Performance, on by default)

Serves Google Fonts from your own site, so your visitors no longer connect to Google to get them. The option “Serve Google Fonts from your own site instead of from Google” (Cache & Performance → Files) is on as soon as the module is turned on, and only acts on pages that already link to Google Fonts. In the background, your server downloads the stylesheet and the font files from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, then keeps them. Google receives your server’s IP address and the names of the fonts requested; nothing about your visitors is sent. Untick the option to stop it.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

YouTube thumbnails (Cache & Performance, on by default)

On pages that already embed a YouTube video, the option “Show a clickable thumbnail instead of loading the full YouTube player” (Cache & Performance → Media) replaces the player with the video’s thumbnail, which the visitor’s browser loads from i.ytimg.com, a YouTube server. The player itself loads only if the visitor clicks. YouTube therefore receives the visitor’s IP address when the thumbnail loads; without the option, the embedded player connects to YouTube as soon as the page opens. Untick the option to keep the original player.

Google (YouTube): Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

IAB Europe Global Vendor List (Cookie Banner)

Used only if you tick “Programmatic advertising compatibility (IAB TCF v2.2)” in Cookie Banner → Advanced; it is off by default. Once a day, your server downloads the public list of advertising vendors from vendor-list.consensu.org. Nothing about your site or your visitors is sent: IAB Europe only sees your server’s IP address.

IAB Europe: Transparency & Consent Framework, Privacy Policy.

OpenStreetMap (Calendar)

Map tiles, on by default: when an event’s venue has map coordinates, the event page shows a map whose images (tiles) the visitor’s browser loads from tile.openstreetmap.org. OpenStreetMap receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details and your site’s address as the referrer. The venue editing screen loads the same tiles in your own browser. To remove the map from event pages, untick “Venue map” in Calendar → Events → Calendar display.

Address lookup (Nominatim): when you click “Locate from address” on a venue, or geocode venues with WP-CLI, the venue’s address (street, city, postal code, region, country) is sent to nominatim.openstreetmap.org to find its coordinates.

OpenStreetMap Foundation: Nominatim Usage Policy, Tile Usage Policy, Privacy Policy.

Remote backups (Backup & Restore)

Copies your backups off your server. Used only once you choose a destination and fill in its connection details in Backup & Restore → Settings → Remote Storage. After each finished backup, every archive of the set is uploaded there. The archives hold what you chose to back up: the database, with everything your site stores in it (user accounts, form entries and so on), and your plugins, themes and uploads. When you ask for it, the plugin also lists archives there and downloads them back; if you turn on remote retention, it deletes the oldest ones.

  • Dropbox, Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive: you connect your own account on the provider’s sign-in page. Dropbox: Terms, Privacy Policy. Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Microsoft: Services Agreement, Privacy Statement.
  • pCloud: Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy.
  • Amazon S3 or another S3-compatible storage (the endpoint you enter decides which). Amazon Web Services: Service Terms, Privacy Notice. Any other S3-compatible provider: its own terms apply.
  • WebDAV and SFTP: the archives go to the server whose address you enter, whether your own or a hosted one such as Nextcloud or kDrive; the terms of whoever runs it apply.

Form webhooks (Forms)

Sends each accepted submission to an address you choose, for tools such as Zapier, Make or n8n. Used only for a form whose “Webhook URL” you fill in, in that form’s settings. Your server sends that address, as JSON, the form’s ID and title, the time of the submission and every submitted field, with signed links to any uploaded files and, on a paid form, the payment information. A failed attempt is retried once. The service behind the address is your choice, and its own terms apply.

Failure alerts to Slack, Discord or Microsoft Teams (SMTP Mailer)

Used only if you tick “Alert me when an email fails to send” in SMTP Mailer → Configuration and enter a webhook address; only Slack, Discord and Microsoft Teams addresses are accepted. When an email fails, at most once every 15 minutes, the alert sends the site name, the recipient address or addresses, the subject, the error message and a link to the email log in your dashboard.

Slack: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Discord: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Microsoft Teams: Services Agreement, Privacy Statement.

Email providers (SMTP Mailer)

SMTP Mailer sends your site’s emails through the relays you set up: Brevo, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES or any other SMTP server. Once a relay is set up, every email your site sends (recipients, subject, content and attachments) passes through …
sections.installation:
1. Upload the blaminhor-essentials folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to “Blaminhor Essentials” in the admin menu.
  4. Turn on the features you need.
sections.faq:
Will activating all features slow down my site?

Each module only runs its own code when activated. A disabled module registers no hooks of its own, enqueues no assets and runs no queries of its own; only a small shared core always loads.

Is it really free?

Yes, genuinely free. Every module and every feature ships in the single free download — no expiring trial, no ads in your dashboard, nothing held back for a paywall. I don’t track you and I don’t sell your data. If it saves you time, a kind review is all I ask.

What are the requirements?

WordPress 6.2 or newer and PHP 8.1 or newer. It runs fine on standard shared hosting: heavy jobs like backups and link scans are processed in small batches to avoid timeouts, and no background service or special server access is required.

Can I replace multiple plugins with this one?

Yes, that’s the main goal. Blaminhor Essentials can replace Redirection, Yoast/Rank Math, WP Mail SMTP, UpdraftPlus, Duplicate Post, User Role Editor, Limit Login Attempts, WP 2FA, and many others.

Will it conflict with my existing SEO, cache or SMTP plugin?

Every module is off by default and independent, so installing the plugin changes nothing until you switch something on. The one thing to avoid is running two plugins that do the same job — two SEO plugins, or two page caches — since they can clash. The clean path is to import your data into the matching module, then deactivate the old plugin.

How do I migrate my data from other plugins?

Several modules include import features, so you don’t lose your existing setup:
– SEO: Import titles, descriptions and keywords from Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO.
– SMTP: Import from WP Mail SMTP, Post SMTP or Easy WP SMTP.
– Redirections: Import from the Redirection plugin, Safe Redirect Manager or a CSV file.
– Post Types Order: Import your saved term order from Custom Taxonomy Order.
– Favicon: Import an existing favicon set from Favicon by RealFaviconGenerator, or from the WordPress Site Icon.
– User Role Editor: Import roles and custom capabilities from the standalone User Role Editor plugin, or from a JSON export.

Does the plugin send my data to external servers?

Only through features you turn on. There is no telemetry and no usage tracking, and every module stays off until you switch it on. Data leaves your site when you use a feature built on an outside service: payments (Stripe), CAPTCHA (Google reCAPTCHA or Cloudflare Turnstile), remote backups (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, pCloud, S3, WebDAV, SFTP), form webhooks, email delivery through your SMTP provider and its failure alerts, the Cloudflare integration, PageSpeed audits, calendar imports, venue address lookups, external link checks, the advertising vendor list of the Cookie Banner, and the error reports and feedback emails you choose to send me. Most of these also need your own account details or an option you tick.

Three features start as soon as their module is turned on. The Calendar venue map loads OpenStreetMap tiles in your visitors’ browsers; untick “Venue map” in Calendar → Events → Calendar display to stop it. Cache & Performance downloads Google Fonts to your server and shows YouTube thumbnails in place of embedded players: both cut down what your visitors send to Google, and each has its own option to switch it off. The External services section lists every service, what it receives and when.

Does the plugin change files on my server?

Only where a feature cannot work otherwise. Besides its own folders (wp-content/blaminhor-essentials and wp-content/uploads/blaminhor-essentials, which hold backups, cached pages and generated files), it touches these files:

  • Cache & Performance installs wp-content/advanced-cache.php, adds the WP_CACHE line to wp-config.php and, on servers that read .htaccess (Apache, LiteSpeed), writes its browser-cache and compression rules to .htaccess in blocks marked “Blaminhor Essentials Cache”. Turning the module off removes all three: wp-config.php goes back to what it was, and if the module had replaced another plugin’s advanced-cache.php, that file is handed back while its plugin is still active.
  • Downloads writes a block marked “Blaminhor Essentials Downloads” to .htaccess, only if you turn on the locking of direct file links. Turning the option or the module off removes it; if .htaccess cannot be written at that moment, the plugin tells you which block to delete by hand.
  • Favicon Generator copies favicon.ico to your WordPress folder, only if no favicon.ico is there yet. Turning the module off leaves it in place: it goes when you click Remove Favicon, or when you delete the plugin with “Delete all data on uninstall” turned on, and even then only if it is still the file the module made.
  • Fatal Error Recovery keeps a fingerprint of your recovery key in a blaminhor-recovery file at the root of wp-content.

Deactivating the plugin runs the same clean-up as turning each module off, so the Cache and Downloads changes are removed; they come back when you reactivate it. Deleting the plugin always removes the .htaccess blocks, the Cache files and the recovery key file, whatever your data setting.

What exactly is sent if I turn on error reports?

That option lives in Fatal Error Recovery → Settings and is off until you tick it. Once on, an error raised inside a Blaminhor Essentials file is emailed to me so I can fix it; errors from other plugins or from your theme are never sent. A report contains the error message, the file and line inside the plugin, and the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions. File paths, email addresses, IP addresses and credentials are stripped out first, and your site address is never included — only a one-way identifier that cannot be traced back to your site. The same error is reported once per plugin version, five reports per version at most. Untick the option and everything stops immediately.

What happens to my settings if I deactivate or uninstall the plugin?

Your data is safe by default. Deactivating keeps every setting untouched, so you can switch the plugin back on right where you left off. Even deleting the plugin keeps your settings and data unless you first turn on the “Delete all data on uninstall” option — and your posts, pages and media are never touched either way. If you do opt in, uninstalling cleans up the plugin’s own options, tables and files so nothing is left behind.

If I turn off a module, do I lose its data?

No. Turning a module off only stops it from running — your redirects, SEO meta, form entries and settings are all kept, so you can switch it back on later exactly as it was. Data is only removed if you delete the whole plugin with the “Delete all data on uninstall” option enabled.

Can I back up my entire site?

Yes. The Backup module creates separate archives for database, plugins, themes and uploads. You can schedule automatic backups (daily, weekly, monthly) and set retention limits.

What happens if a backup restore goes wrong?

The plugin automatically creates a safety backup before any restore. If something goes wrong, you can undo it with one click.

Does the SMTP module support multiple providers?

Yes. You can configure multiple relays with automatic fallback. If the primary one fails, it tries the next in your list.

Can I duplicate Elementor/Divi pages?

Yes. The Content Duplicator fully supports all major page builders, including Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Brizy and Oxygen.

Can I control which user roles can access certain features?

Yes. For example, the Post Types Order module lets you choose which roles can reorder content (Administrator, Editor or Author), and the User Role Editor gives you fine-grained control over every capability.

What if my site crashes after a plugin update?

The Fatal Error Recovery module detects PHP fatal errors and gives you a secret recovery URL to deactivate the problematic plugin — no FTP access needed.

What languages is the plugin available in?

Eleven. English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Russian and Turkish are fully translated; Dutch and Indonesian are partially translated, with anything untranslated falling back to English.

Does the plugin work with multisite?

Yes, on a per-site basis. Each site keeps its own settings, its own database tables and its own backups (Backup, Domain Changer and Database Optimizer store archives in a separate per-site folder), so sites stay fully isolated. Network activation, deactivation and uninstall apply cleanly to every site, and sites created later are set up automatically. Two notes: server-level browser cache and GZIP rules live in the shared root .htaccess and are managed by a network administrator (PHP page caching still applies on every site); and there is no central Network Admin screen yet, so you configure each site from its own dashboard.

How can I get support?

Email me at hi+wp@blaminhor.com or visit wp.blaminhor.com. You can also use the feedback form on the plugin dashboard.
sections.changelog:
2.8.8

  • Fixed: SEO/GEO – Importing from Yoast, Rank Math or All in One SEO no longer writes “Array” as a title when a source field holds structured data.
  • Fixed: Redirections – Importing from the Redirection plugin keeps the rule that was redirecting when two share a source, and imports the rules of disabled groups inactive.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – A leftover cache file that cannot be deleted is retried once an hour instead of on every request, which filled the log.

2.8.7

  • Added: Core – Calendar, Forms, Downloads, Maintenance and SMTP Mailer data join the WordPress export and erasure tools, even with the module off.
  • Added: Core – After a change of the WordPress security keys, a notice lists the saved passwords and tokens to type again.
  • Added: Cookie Banner – The banner links to your privacy and cookie policies, shows “Do Not Sell or Share” with the US preset, and blocked embeds explain why.
  • Improved: Calendar – Appointments, registrations and waitlists no longer keep a coded visitor IP, and old bookings can be anonymised after a delay you set.
  • Improved: Core – The readme lists every outside service a module can contact, and the map, CAPTCHA and feedback settings say what they send.
  • Fixed: Core – Sites running PHP 8.1 no longer stop with a fatal error when Domain Changer or Backup & Restore is active.
  • Fixed: Login Security – An account whose two-factor secret can no longer be read is refused with an explanation instead of signing in on its password alone.
  • Fixed: Core – Address checks for webhooks, imports and feeds refuse more private addresses, and proxy headers can no longer be forged via IPv6-form IPv4.
  • Fixed: Maintenance – A forged forwarded address can no longer bypass the IP whitelist, which now matches real visitors behind a proxy or CDN.
  • Fixed: Hide Login Page – A forged wp-login.php request posing as a protected-post password can no longer reach the login form.
  • Fixed: Downloads – An unknown role no longer makes a restricted file public, and file locking survives reactivation, restores and address changes.
  • Fixed: User Role Editor – Saving keeps capabilities set elsewhere, such as WooCommerce shop manager rights, and roles with capitals in their slug are found.
  • Fixed: Forms – Editors can no longer edit or delete forms outside the Forms screens, and the CAPTCHA is checked before any upload is saved.
  • Fixed: Calendar – A paid booking, sign-up or rental is recorded even if the visitor never returns from Stripe, and a paid series is never refunded twice.
  • Fixed: Forms – Amounts are kept as typed; an unreadable amount or Stripe key refuses the submission instead of charging another sum or nothing.
  • Fixed: Core – Payments are all settled during busy sales, and a refund made despite a timeout is no longer reported as failed.
  • Fixed: Calendar – No double booking around midnight UTC, and recurring, multi-day, all-day and iCal events keep their dates and time zones.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – A relay password that can no longer be decrypted is never sent empty: the email fails and is retried later.
  • Fixed: Backup & Restore – Backups survive proxy timeouts and host interruptions, and stopping one leaves no partial file nor deletes a finished one.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – Excluded URLs, cookies and user agents bypass cached pages, and no page is served truncated or replaced by an encoded parameter.
  • Fixed: Cookie Banner – Google Consent Mode and TCF follow the visitor’s real choice, and withdrawal removes every consent cookie.
  • Fixed: SEO/GEO – The sitemap leaves out noindexed content, and Elementor saves no longer lose or overwrite SEO settings.
  • Fixed: Anti-Spam – Real visitors are no longer taken for bots: WooCommerce My Account customers get through and wpDiscuz comments stay out of spam.
  • Fixed: Domain Changer – Changing example.co no longer rewrites example.com links, and a change stopped by a time, memory or disk limit can be undone.
  • Fixed: Database Optimizer – The dashboard Optimize DB button no longer empties trash or spam without review.
  • Fixed: HTTPS Redirect – “Disable HTTPS” on the recovery page also stops HSTS and the admin redirect, so a site stuck on HTTP is no longer locked out.
    Every change of this release, line by line, is in changelog.txt shipped with the plugin.

2.8.6

  • Fixed: Favicon Generator – Generated favicons are served again instead of answering 403 Forbidden on Apache servers.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – Locally hosted Google Fonts are served again instead of answering 403 Forbidden on Apache servers.

2.8.5

  • Added: SMTP Mailer – Beta: emails that no relay could send are kept encrypted for up to 72 hours and sent again automatically; you can turn it off.
  • Added: SMTP Mailer – A Retry queue tab lists the waiting emails, with Send now, Remove and Empty the queue.
  • Added: SMTP Mailer – The dashboard warns when emails were dropped after all their retries failed.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – A relay that accepts the connection but never answers no longer stalls email sending for up to five minutes.

2.8.4

  • Improved: Login Security – The two-factor reminder explains why every admin page sends you to your profile, links to the setup section and opens at the top.

2.8.3

  • Added: Forms – The auto-reply gets an optional reply-to address, so replies reach the contact you choose.
  • Improved: Calendar – Replying to a new booking, sign-up or reservation notification now writes to the visitor.
  • Fixed: Forms – The auto-reply no longer exposes the site admin email as its Reply-To; replies go to the sending address.
  • Fixed: Forms – Saving a form keeps you on the tab you were editing instead of jumping back to Fields.

2.8.2

  • Improved: Core – Admin screens adapt to phones and tablets: page titles, tables, settings menus and forms fit the screen width.
  • Improved: Fatal Error Recovery – Crash reports hide file paths, email addresses and IPv6 addresses that appear inside stack traces.

2.8.1

  • Added: Core – WP-CLI now covers every module in full: each setting can be read and changed, and missing actions such as SEO scoring are added.
  • Added: Calendar – wp blaminhor calendar creates, updates and deletes events, venues and organizers with the admin screen’s checks, and edits promo codes.
  • Added: Forms – wp blaminhor forms creates, updates and deletes forms and manages the CAPTCHA, upload and Stripe settings.
  • Added: Anti-Spam, Image Sizes, Mute Core Emails, Cache & Performance – Their settings and actions, such as Cloudflare and critical CSS, work from the command line.
  • Improved: Core – Command-line actions that delete data or notify visitors ask for confirmation unless --yes is given, and Advanced > WP-CLI lists every command.
  • Fixed: Core – WP-CLI settings commands no longer switch off options they were not asked to change in Database Optimizer, Domain Changer, Cookie Banner and three other modules.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – Importing settings keeps the per-page asset rules, Cloudflare originals can be restored, and clearing one critical CSS variant keeps the others.
  • Fixed: Calendar – Ticket tier names with accents are saved intact, deleting a venue clears it from draft and trashed events, and the navigation buttons take the hover colour.
  • Fixed: Backup & Restore – Importing a bundle never installs another site’s safety archive as the undo point, and concurrent restores and scheduled backups are locked out.
  • Fixed: Forms – Deleting a form by any means also deletes its entries and uploaded files.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer, User Role Editor, HTTPS Redirect – Reset emails are never resent masked, snapshots restore the one chosen, and certificate alerts follow the switch.

2.8.0

  • Improved: Calendar, Forms, Login Security, Downloads – The Beta labels, banners and warnings are gone: the four modules are now stable.
  • Improved: Core – Module settings pages load about 8 KB less JavaScript, as the dashboard-only code now loads on the dashboard alone.
  • Improved: SEO/GEO – Key Takeaways and Table of Contents load a 1 KB stylesheet instead of 170 KB on the public site, and show their intended border and spacing.
  • Fixed: Post Types Order – The drag-and-drop sort screens on content lists now load their colours and spacing.

2.7.5

  • Fixed: Core – Security: on multisite, backups, roles, plugin recovery and domain changes, including switching those modules on or off, are reserved to network administrators.
  • Fixed: Core – Settings pages behave as shown: Cancel really discards changes, errors stay on screen, and turning a module off cleans up after it, scheduled tasks included.
  • Fixed: Core – A damaged setting falls back to its defaults instead of taking the site down, and errors reach the server’s PHP log even when the plugin log is off.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – Security: no readable copy of wp-config.php is left behind, and turning the module off restores the previous drop-in and WP_CACHE line.
  • Fixed: Cache & Performance – Forms, bookings and consent keep working on cached pages, and Defer or Delay JS never run a script before the library it needs.
  • Fixed: Hide Login Page – The secret login address no longer leaks through redirects, /wp-register.php or protected-post forms, and password resets work on multisite.
  • Fixed: Cookie Banner – Trackers stay blocked until consent on cached or very large pages, and the cookie policy lists only the services your site uses.
  • Fixed: SEO/GEO – Security: structured data can no longer carry injected code, public types such as events stay indexed, and robots.txt names the right sitemap.
  • Fixed: Backup & Restore – Restoring from another address keeps this site’s settings, and existing backups stay visible after a reinstall or a busy first request.
  • Fixed: Downloads – Security: protected files can no longer be reached through an altered or direct link, and file locking works on multisite.
  • Fixed: Login Security – Two-factor checks and login limits hold under parallel requests and behind proxies, and new-login alerts wait for the second factor.
  • Fixed: Calendar – Venue, organizer, category and tag pages open again, paid bookings are recorded once, and sign-ups work without JavaScript.
  • Fixed: Forms – Forms are styled with block themes, uploaded files stay private, and zero-decimal currencies are charged correctly.
  • Fixed: Redirections – Non-Latin, case-sensitive and plain regex rules match correctly, the visitor’s query string is kept, and the 404 log only records real 404s.
  • Fixed: Image Sizes – Regenerating thumbnails starts from the original image and keeps the ones your content still uses.
  • Fixed: Post Types Order – Your order no longer overrides sorts chosen by visitors or search, and saving it for the first time keeps the site’s current order.
  • Fixed: Core – Many smaller fixes across Anti-Spam, Broken Links, Classic Editor, Content Duplicator, Database Optimizer, Disable Comments, SMTP Mailer and User Role Editor.
  • Improved: Core – A CDN or load balancer on public addresses can be declared in Settings, so attempt limits apply to each visitor.
  • Removed: SEO/GEO – Sitemap pings to search engines, which no longer accept them.

2.7.4

  • Improved: Backup & Restore – A backup too large to arrive in one file can be downloaded volume by volume, and a single volume can be uploaded back to restore it.
  • Added: Backup & Restore – A download test reports what your server really sends: the announced size, whether an interrupted transfer can resume, and the measured speed.
  • Improved: Core – An interrupted download resumes where it stopped instead of risking a corrupted file, and a long transfer no longer holds up the rest of the admin.

2.7.3

  • Added: SMTP Mailer – Checks the sender domain’s SPF, DKIM and DMARC records against your provider, so an unauthorised relay is flagged before your mail quietly disappears.
  • Improved: SMTP Mailer – Testing a relay reports what that relay answered, in the server’s own words and with the SMTP conversation on hand, never the next relay’s.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – The email log matches what it actually keeps, shows a test message as soon as it is sent, and reloads on demand.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – Adding, editing or removing a relay no longer reloads the page or drops settings you have not saved, and a refresh never repeats the action.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – Editing a relay you had disabled no longer switches it back on when you save.
  • Fixed: SMTP Mailer – An imported relay arrives switched off with its sender address kept, and importing never replaces the default sender of a site that already has one.

2.7.2

  • Fixed: Maintenance – Administrators keep access to the front-end while maintenance or coming-soon mode is on, as the Access tab states.

2.7.1

  • Fixed: Backup & Restore – Downloading a large backup no longer fails at the very end, and the saved archive opens correctly.
  • Improved: Backup & Restore – Backup downloads can be paused and resumed, and one that starts before your session ends finishes on its own.
  • Fixed: Content Duplicator – The “Original title” option now works: it was listed in the settings but never applied, so the title was always copied.
  • Added: Core – WP-CLI now covers every module, from download counters and link scans to database backups, consent exports and per-file access rules.
  • Fixed: Core – WP-CLI no longer clears settings it was not asked to touch, among them the off-site backup destination, certificate expiry monitoring and delivery-failure alerts.
  • Fixed: Core – WP-CLI commands that stopped with an error now work, including single-URL checks, item reordering and favicon generation.

2.7.0

  • New module: Downloads (Beta) – Know what actually gets downloaded from your media library, and decide who can:
    • Total and unique download counts per file, with robots, link previews and repeat clicks filtered out, and no visitor address ever stored.
    • Documents save to disk instead of opening in a browser tab.
    • Any file restricted to signed-in visitors, to chosen roles, or behind a password.
    • Direct file requests routed through the counted link, so links already shared stay covered.
  • Added: Login Security – Copies the authenticator key and the backup codes to the clipboard in one click.
  • Improved: Login Security – Opens on Statistics so recent sign-in activity comes first, with settings next.
  • Improved: Login Security – The two-factor tab now shows whether your own account is protected and links straight to where you set it up.
  • Fixed: Core – Saving settings from a tab now returns to that tab instead of the first one, and reloading the page no longer asks to resend the form.
  • Fixed: Core – The “Settings saved” confirmation is no longer lost when saving Broken Links, Database Optimizer, User Role Editor or Cookie Banner settings.
  • Fixed: Anti-Spam – Saving from the email protection tab no longer sends you back to the first tab.
  • Fixed: Login Security – Turning off a two-factor method now hides it from the profile screen as described, and it can no longer be set up once disabled.
  • Fixed: Login Security – The sign-in challenge no longer overlaps the trust-this-browser checkbox with the confirmation button.

2.6.0

  • New module: Login Security (Beta) – Everything that guards the front door, on your own site with no external service:
    • Brute-force throttling across the login form, XML-RPC, the REST API and application passwords.
    • Two-factor sign-in: authenticator app, security key or passkey, emailed code and single-use backup codes, with trusted browsers.
    • A password policy and sign-in alerts, plus a privacy-friendly journal of every attempt with hashed addresses.
    • WP-CLI unlock and second-factor reset, an IP allowlist and a wp-config.php switch so you can never lock yourself out.
  • Improved: Core – Confirms compatibility with WordPress 7.1, including the always-iframed post editor, client-side media processing and the persistent editor toolbar.
  • Improved: Hide Login Page – Points to the Login Security module for brute-force throttling, two-factor authentication and a sign-in journal.

The full detail of every change in 2.8.7, and older versions (2.5.14 and earlier), are in changelog.txt shipped with the plugin.

short_description: All-in-one WordPress toolkit: SEO, cache, backup, SMTP, 301 redirects, GDPR cookie banner, 2FA login security, forms and events. 26 free modules.
description:
One plugin to replace twenty. Free forever.

I was tired of my WordPress installs looking like a graveyard of single-purpose plugins — one for SEO, one for cache, one for SMTP, one for redirects, one for backups. Each one with its own dashboard, its own freemium dance. So I built Blaminhor Essentials — and I never sell your data.

Why this plugin exists:

  • Every WordPress essential under one roof. SEO, cache, SMTP, backup, cookie banner, contact forms, calendar, anti-spam, login security, downloads, redirections, broken links, duplicator, database optimizer, domain changer, fatal error recovery, favicon, HTTPS redirect, hide login, image sizes, maintenance mode, mute core emails, post types order, user role editor, classic editor, disable comments. Switch on what you use today; the rest stays out of your way until the day you need it.
  • Your existing data comes with you. Switching does not mean starting over: built-in importers for Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, WP Mail SMTP, Post SMTP, Easy WP SMTP, Redirection, Safe Redirect Manager, Custom Taxonomy Order, Favicon by RealFaviconGenerator, and the standalone User Role Editor. The dedicated plugins you’ve stacked one by one over the years, now in a single coherent toolkit.
  • No tax for what you don’t use. Each module is independent: an inactive one registers no hooks of its own, enqueues no assets and runs no queries of its own. Only a small shared core always loads, so beyond it you’re only paying — in memory and milliseconds — for the features you actually turned on.
  • Rebuilt on modern PHP. Since version 2, every module has been re-engineered from the ground up to take full advantage of PHP 8 — strict types, enums and value objects — for tighter security and faster, leaner execution.
  • Free. All features above are free. No tracking, no telemetry.
  • Translated in 11 languages. English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese, Russian, Turkish, Dutch, Indonesian.
  • You can email me anytime. hi+wp@blaminhor.com

Available Features — 26 modules:

Performance

  • Cache & Performance — Page cache, asset optimization and lazy load, plus a Web Vitals dashboard and an auto-pilot that benchmarks each speed option on your own pages.

SEO & Links

  • SEO/GEO — Meta titles and descriptions with SERP preview, XML sitemaps, per-type indexing control, and one-click import from Yoast, Rank Math or All in One SEO.
  • Redirections — Simple or regex redirects (301, 302, 307, 410, 451) with hit counters, slug-change detection, and CSV / plugin import (Redirection, Safe Redirect Manager).
  • Broken Links — Scan posts, pages and custom post types for dead internal and external links, with live results and one-click fixes.

Emails

  • SMTP Mailer — Reliable delivery through 12+ providers (Brevo, SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES…) with automatic relay fallback, a retry queue for emails that fail (Beta), logging, and import from WP Mail SMTP, Post SMTP or Easy WP SMTP.
  • Mute Core Emails — Silence WordPress automatic notifications (updates, new users, password changes, comments) individually.

Security & Maintenance

  • Cookie Banner — Self-hosted consent banner that blocks tracking scripts and embeds until visitors agree, with GDPR/CCPA/LGPD presets, Consent Mode v2, and a 13-month consent log.
  • Anti-Spam — Block spam bots on the comment, login, registration and password forms with a hidden honeypot trap, and encode the email addresses shown on your site so harvesters cannot read them — no CAPTCHA, no external service.
  • Login Security — Lock out brute-force attempts on every sign-in route (login form, XML-RPC, REST API, application passwords) before the password is checked, add two-factor authentication (authenticator app, security key or passkey, emailed code, single-use backup codes) with trusted browsers, alert on sign-ins from unfamiliar devices, enforce a password policy per role, and keep a journal of every attempt with addresses stored hashed. Entirely local, no external service.
  • Hide Login Page — Replace wp-login.php with a custom URL and block bots probing the default login.
  • HTTPS Redirect — Force HTTPS site-wide with optional mixed-content fixing and an HSTS header.
  • Fatal Error Recovery — Recover a crashed site from a secret URL by disabling the culprit plugin, with no FTP access.
  • Maintenance — Show a Coming Soon (200) or Maintenance (503) page, with role and IP whitelisting.
  • User Role Editor — Create, clone and edit roles and capabilities, with per-user overrides, JSON import/export and one-click import from the standalone User Role Editor plugin.

Database & Migration

  • Backup & Restore — Scheduled backups of files and database as separate archives, with a safety backup and one-click undo before every restore.
  • Database Optimizer — Clean revisions, transients, spam and orphaned data on a schedule, with an at-a-glance size and overhead overview.
  • Domain Changer — Change your site domain and update every database reference, including serialized data, in one click.

Content & Media

  • Calendar — Publish events with recurrence, venues, organizers, calendar views, iCal import and RSVP, and run a full booking system for appointments and resource rentals with reminders and Stripe payments.
  • Forms — Accessible drag-and-drop contact forms with entries stored in the database, no-CAPTCHA spam protection, and GDPR controls.
  • Downloads — Count how many times each media library file is downloaded, and how many distinct people downloaded it, without recreating your files as anything else. Make documents save instead of opening in a tab, restrict a file to signed-in visitors, chosen roles or a password, and optionally route direct file requests through the counted link so links already shared are covered too. Robots, link previews and repeat clicks are filtered out, and no visitor address is ever stored.
  • Content Duplicator — Clone any post, page or custom post type with all fields, taxonomies and child posts; supports every major page builder.
  • Classic Editor & Widgets — Restore the classic editor and/or the classic widgets screen, independently.
  • Image Sizes — Disable unused thumbnail sizes, register custom ones, and regenerate existing images.
  • Favicon Generator — Generate every favicon format (PNG, Apple Touch, Android, Windows tiles) from a single square image, or import an existing set from Favicon by RealFaviconGenerator or the WordPress Site Icon.
  • Post Types Order — Reorder posts, pages, custom post types and taxonomies with drag and drop, and import an existing term order from Custom Taxonomy Order.
  • Disable Comments — Remove the comment system site-wide and hide it from the admin, reversibly.

External services

Every module is off by default, and a module that is off contacts nothing. This section lists every outside service a module can connect to, what it receives and when. Most of them start only once you enter your own account details or tick a specific option. Three start as soon as their module is turned on, and are marked “on by default” below: the Calendar venue map, and the self-hosted Google Fonts and YouTube thumbnails of Cache & Performance.

Stripe (Forms and Calendar payments)

Takes online payments for paid forms, paid event sign-ups, paid appointments and resource rentals. It is used only once you enter a Stripe secret key on the Forms settings page (Payments section), and only for the forms, events, services or resources you give a price.

When a visitor starts a payment, your server sends Stripe the amount, the currency, a short description (the form’s payment label, or the event, service or resource name), the addresses on your site the visitor comes back to, and two internal references: a random payment token and the kind of purchase. The visitor then types their card details, and any contact details Stripe asks for, on Stripe’s own payment page; none of it passes through your site. While a payment is pending, your server checks its status with Stripe when the visitor comes back, and otherwise once an hour. If a payment arrives for something that can no longer be recorded (a slot taken in the meantime, for example), your server asks Stripe to refund it.

Stripe: Services Agreement, Privacy Policy.

Google reCAPTCHA and Cloudflare Turnstile (Forms)

Optional CAPTCHA challenges against spam. Forms already blocks spam without them: a CAPTCHA is used only if you enter the provider’s keys on the Forms settings page and add a CAPTCHA field to a form.

On a page that shows such a form, the visitor’s browser loads the provider’s script from google.com or challenges.cloudflare.com. The provider therefore receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details and whatever its script collects, under its own policy. When the form is sent, your server sends the provider the challenge token and your secret key so it can check the answer; the plugin does not add the visitor’s IP address to that check.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Cloudflare: Website Terms, Privacy Policy.

Google PageSpeed Insights (Cache & Performance)

Measures how fast a page loads. It runs only when you start a PageSpeed audit in Cache & Performance → Performance, or with the matching WP-CLI command. Your server sends Google the address of the page to audit and, if you saved one, your PageSpeed API key; Google then loads that public page to measure it. Testing a key sends one request with the key and a sample address.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Cloudflare API (Cache & Performance)

Keeps Cloudflare’s cache in step with your site. It is used only if you tick “Enable Cloudflare integration” in Cache & Performance → CDN and enter an API token and a Zone ID. With your token, your server sends Cloudflare the addresses of the pages to refresh when you publish, update or trash content, a request to empty the whole zone when you empty the site cache, and, when you click the matching buttons, reads and changes of your zone’s settings (Development Mode, recommended settings).

Cloudflare: Website Terms, Privacy Policy.

Google Fonts (Cache & Performance, on by default)

Serves Google Fonts from your own site, so your visitors no longer connect to Google to get them. The option “Serve Google Fonts from your own site instead of from Google” (Cache & Performance → Files) is on as soon as the module is turned on, and only acts on pages that already link to Google Fonts. In the background, your server downloads the stylesheet and the font files from fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, then keeps them. Google receives your server’s IP address and the names of the fonts requested; nothing about your visitors is sent. Untick the option to stop it.

Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

YouTube thumbnails (Cache & Performance, on by default)

On pages that already embed a YouTube video, the option “Show a clickable thumbnail instead of loading the full YouTube player” (Cache & Performance → Media) replaces the player with the video’s thumbnail, which the visitor’s browser loads from i.ytimg.com, a YouTube server. The player itself loads only if the visitor clicks. YouTube therefore receives the visitor’s IP address when the thumbnail loads; without the option, the embedded player connects to YouTube as soon as the page opens. Untick the option to keep the original player.

Google (YouTube): Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

IAB Europe Global Vendor List (Cookie Banner)

Used only if you tick “Programmatic advertising compatibility (IAB TCF v2.2)” in Cookie Banner → Advanced; it is off by default. Once a day, your server downloads the public list of advertising vendors from vendor-list.consensu.org. Nothing about your site or your visitors is sent: IAB Europe only sees your server’s IP address.

IAB Europe: Transparency & Consent Framework, Privacy Policy.

OpenStreetMap (Calendar)

Map tiles, on by default: when an event’s venue has map coordinates, the event page shows a map whose images (tiles) the visitor’s browser loads from tile.openstreetmap.org. OpenStreetMap receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details and your site’s address as the referrer. The venue editing screen loads the same tiles in your own browser. To remove the map from event pages, untick “Venue map” in Calendar → Events → Calendar display.

Address lookup (Nominatim): when you click “Locate from address” on a venue, or geocode venues with WP-CLI, the venue’s address (street, city, postal code, region, country) is sent to nominatim.openstreetmap.org to find its coordinates.

OpenStreetMap Foundation: Nominatim Usage Policy, Tile Usage Policy, Privacy Policy.

Remote backups (Backup & Restore)

Copies your backups off your server. Used only once you choose a destination and fill in its connection details in Backup & Restore → Settings → Remote Storage. After each finished backup, every archive of the set is uploaded there. The archives hold what you chose to back up: the database, with everything your site stores in it (user accounts, form entries and so on), and your plugins, themes and uploads. When you ask for it, the plugin also lists archives there and downloads them back; if you turn on remote retention, it deletes the oldest ones.

  • Dropbox, Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive: you connect your own account on the provider’s sign-in page. Dropbox: Terms, Privacy Policy. Google: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Microsoft: Services Agreement, Privacy Statement.
  • pCloud: Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy.
  • Amazon S3 or another S3-compatible storage (the endpoint you enter decides which). Amazon Web Services: Service Terms, Privacy Notice. Any other S3-compatible provider: its own terms apply.
  • WebDAV and SFTP: the archives go to the server whose address you enter, whether your own or a hosted one such as Nextcloud or kDrive; the terms of whoever runs it apply.

Form webhooks (Forms)

Sends each accepted submission to an address you choose, for tools such as Zapier, Make or n8n. Used only for a form whose “Webhook URL” you fill in, in that form’s settings. Your server sends that address, as JSON, the form’s ID and title, the time of the submission and every submitted field, with signed links to any uploaded files and, on a paid form, the payment information. A failed attempt is retried once. The service behind the address is your choice, and its own terms apply.

Failure alerts to Slack, Discord or Microsoft Teams (SMTP Mailer)

Used only if you tick “Alert me when an email fails to send” in SMTP Mailer → Configuration and enter a webhook address; only Slack, Discord and Microsoft Teams addresses are accepted. When an email fails, at most once every 15 minutes, the alert sends the site name, the recipient address or addresses, the subject, the error message and a link to the email log in your dashboard.

Slack: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Discord: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy. Microsoft Teams: Services Agreement, Privacy Statement.

Email providers (SMTP Mailer)

SMTP Mailer sends your site’s emails through the relays you set up: Brevo, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES or any other SMTP server. Once a relay is set up, every email your site sends (recipients, subject, content and attachments) passes through …

upgrade_notice.2.8.8: Fixes imports from Yoast, Rank Math and All in One SEO writing the word Array as a title, and imports from Redirection keeping the wrong rule when two share a source; update before importing from any of them.
upgrade_notice.2.8.7: Fixes a fatal error on PHP 8.1 with Domain Changer or Backup active; an account whose authenticator app secret can no longer be read is now refused at sign-in until an admin resets it; Maintenance sign-ups older than a year are purged.
upgrade_notice.2.8.6: Fixes favicons and locally hosted Google Fonts answering 403 Forbidden on Apache servers; update if your generated favicon or self-hosted fonts do not load.
upgrade_notice.2.8.5: SMTP Mailer can now keep emails that no relay could send and retry them for up to 72 hours (Beta, on by default, can be turned off); update if a relay outage has ever cost you emails.
upgrade_notice.2.8.4: Login Security's two-factor reminder now explains why admin pages send you to your profile and links straight to the setup section; update if you require two-factor for any role.
upgrade_notice.2.8.3: The Forms auto-reply no longer shows your WordPress admin email when visitors reply, so update now if you use auto-replies; it also gains an optional reply-to address.
upgrade_notice.2.8.2: Admin screens now fit phones and tablets, and Fatal Error Recovery crash reports hide more private details such as file paths and email addresses.
upgrade_notice.2.8.1: WP-CLI now covers every module, with calendar events, venues and forms manageable from the command line, plus fixes to settings import, Cloudflare restore and Backup restore.
upgrade_notice.2.8.0: Calendar, Forms, Login Security and Downloads leave Beta. Module settings pages load less JavaScript, and Key Takeaways and Table of Contents blocks are styled correctly on the public site.
upgrade_notice.2.7.5: Security and reliability release across all 26 modules. Behaviour changes: SEO/GEO indexes public content types such as events unless you exclude them, Post Types Order respects sorts chosen by visitors, Anti-Spam strict timing needs JavaScript, and sitemap pings are removed.
upgrade_notice.2.7.4: A backup too large to download in one file can now be fetched volume by volume, and a built-in test reports what your server actually sends. An interrupted download resumes where it stopped instead of risking a corrupted archive.
upgrade_notice.2.7.3: Testing an SMTP relay now reports what that relay actually answered instead of always announcing success, and checks whether your sender domain authorises it. Relay changes no longer drop unsaved settings or switch a disabled relay back on.
upgrade_notice.2.7.2: Restores front-end access for administrators while maintenance or coming-soon mode is on: previewing your site no longer shows the maintenance page instead of your content.
upgrade_notice.2.7.1: Fixes large backup downloads, and stops WP-CLI from clearing settings it was not asked to touch — including the off-site backup destination, certificate expiry monitoring and delivery-failure alerts. Adds WP-CLI coverage across every module.
upgrade_notice.2.7.0: New Downloads module (Beta): count total and unique downloads for your media files, force them to save instead of opening, and restrict any file to signed-in visitors, chosen roles or a password. Plus tab-navigation and two-factor fixes across the plugin.
upgrade_notice.2.6.0: New Login Security module (Beta): brute-force throttling across every login route, two-factor sign-in (authenticator app, passkey, email or backup codes), a password policy, sign-in alerts and a privacy-friendly journal — all on your own site, no external service.
upgrade_notice.2.5.14: Patch with security fixes: backups and database exports move to a folder that cannot be guessed from a URL, form webhooks can no longer reach private network addresses, and SVG uploads are always refused. Also fixes restores on hosts that cap PHP execution time.
upgrade_notice.2.5.13: Patch: backups no longer die with a fatal error on hosts that cap PHP execution time — a run now continues over several passes and picks up where it stopped. Also fixes restores failing on those same hosts, and cuts memory use when exporting a large database.
upgrade_notice.2.5.12: Patch: the pre-update backup was never created before WordPress core updates — it now is, whatever starts the update. The retention limit also applies to backups made from the admin screen, and an interrupted backup is flagged instead of being offered for restore.
upgrade_notice.2.5.11: Patch: fixes a fatal error on activation under PHP 8.1, makes imported Yoast, Rank Math and All in One SEO title/description variables render properly, and carries site-wide SEO defaults over during import. Safe maintenance update.
upgrade_notice.2.5.10: Fatal Error Recovery gains a 90-day history of the crashes it caught, dates them in plain language, and can prepare a redacted crash report in one click. It can also report this plugin's own errors to me automatically, if you switch that option on. Fixes fatal errors on URLs without a path.
upgrade_notice.2.5.9: Patch: fixes the Save button staying disabled when your only change in a settings screen is deleting something — like removing a booking time slot or closing an open day in the calendar.
upgrade_notice.2.5.8: Patch: fixes a rare fatal error that could take down the front end when a request arrived with a malformed URL while 301 redirections were active.
upgrade_notice.2.5.7: Patch: the WP-CLI resource list now reports each resource's real stock, and the appointment date in the booking recap follows the site's language rather than the visitor's browser. Safe maintenance update.
upgrade_notice.2.5.6: Security hardening across several modules (SSRF, CSV export safety, multisite capability guard, recovery-key protection), a full WP-CLI command suite, and calendar improvements. Recommended for all sites.
upgrade_notice.2.5.5: The booking calendar's service editor is clearer: each service is its own card with proper on/off toggles, and the online-meeting option only appears — and reads sensibly — for services that can take place online.
upgrade_notice.2.5.4: Patch: venues can show a map on the event page, clients can book a recurring series of appointments, events can sell multiple ticket tiers with promo codes, and both Forms and the Calendar are now fully manageable from WP-CLI.
upgrade_notice.2.5.3: Calendar settings are reorganised into one tab per scheduling type (appointments, events, bookables) with a section menu, and you gain event sign-up approval, a bookable waitlist, and a sign-up cutoff before events.
upgrade_notice.2.5.2: Patch: the client self-service space (reschedule and cancel, no account) is now on by default on new sites, the booking-form consent wording is clearer, and the Calendar settings tabs are tidier — key options stay visible while secondary ones tuck away.
upgrade_notice.2.5.1: Patch release: security and reliability hardening across modules (Fatal Error Recovery, Maintenance, SMTP, User Role Editor, Backup, Calendar), plus Calendar emails and labels that follow your site language and rate-limited public forms.
upgrade_notice.2.5.0: New Calendar module (Beta): publish events with RSVP and run a full online booking system — appointments, resource rentals, reminders and Stripe payments. Plus SFTP backups via SSH key and a clearer, more accessible dashboard. Recommended.

screenshots.caption: Modular dashboard – Enable only the modules you need, organised by category with instant activation.
Cache & Performance – Overview of your whole cache stack, with an auto-pilot that tests each speed option on your real pages.
SEO/GEO – Manage meta titles and descriptions for all your content from one place, with at-a-glance optimisation status.
SMTP Mailer – Send through several relays with automatic fallback when one provider fails.
Backup & Restore – Choose exactly what to back up: database, plugins, themes and uploads.
Database Optimizer – See your database size and overhead, then clean and optimise in one click.
Fatal Error Recovery – Recover a crashed site from a secret recovery URL, with no FTP access.
Image Sizes – Review every registered thumbnail size and disable the ones you do not use.
User Role Editor – Edit capabilities per role, search, and add or clone roles.
Cookie Banner – GDPR consent banner with jurisdiction presets, layout and appearance controls.
